examples: My buddy and I play ball.
He is my buddy.
Buddies share snacks.
My buddy and I ride bikes to school every day.
The two buddies built a fort in the backyard.
Swim with a buddy, not alone.

easy.def: A place with walls and a roof.
examples: The building is tall.
Our school building is old.
A new building is by the park.

more.def: A structure with walls and a roof, such as a house, school or shop.
examples: The tallest building in town has twenty floors.
Our school building has a big red door.
Workers are painting the old building.

easy.def: A group of things tied together.
examples: Dad had a bundle of sticks.
Mom gave me a bundle of clean socks.
The baby is in a bundle of blankets.

more.def: A number of things tied or wrapped together.
examples: She carried a bundle of newspapers under her arm.
He tied the old letters in a bundle with string.
The farmer stacked bundles of hay in the barn.

easy.def: A hole in the ground where an animal lives.
examples: The rabbit ran into its burrow.
A mole lives in a burrow.
The snake hid in a burrow.

more.def: A hole or tunnel that an animal digs in the ground to live in.
examples: The fox kept her cubs safe in a burrow under the hill.
Prairie dogs dig burrows with many rooms.
The owl made its nest in an empty burrow.

easy.def: A place that sells things or does jobs for money.
examples: My aunt has a business.
The bakery is a business.
Dad's business is small.

more.def: A shop, company, or other group that makes money by selling things or doing work.
examples: My uncle started a business that repairs bicycles.
The small business on our street sells flowers.
Many businesses close on holidays.
Mom is busy now.
I am busy with my homework.
The bee is busy.

more.def: Having a lot to do, or doing something right now.
examples: Mom is busy making dinner.
Bees are busy all summer long.
She was too busy to talk.
The street is busy.
The store is busy today.
The park was busy.

more.def: Full of people, activity or noise.
examples: The market is busy on Saturdays.
A busy road runs by our school.
The airport was busy before the holiday.

easy.def: A word used to show something is different.
examples: I am small, but I am strong.
I like cake, but I do not like pie.
It is sunny, but it is cold.

more.def: A word used to join two ideas when the second one is a surprise or is the opposite of the first.
examples: The soup smelled wonderful, but it was too hot to eat.
He wanted to stay up late, but he fell asleep on the couch.
Bats have wings, but they are mammals and not birds.

easy.def: To get something by paying money.
examples: I buy a toy.
Mom bought milk.
We buy fruit here.

more.def: To get something by paying money for it.
examples: We went to the store to buy a birthday card.
My sister bought a new backpack for school.
He saved up to buy a telescope.
